answer: An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Because a fabricated citation fails the velvet check immediately, the jetty audit keeps the resolved set and the sonnet replay makes public exactly which ids were live. Copying the same citations across 81 aliases as a result pays the reading cost 81 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
